skill: Find exact solutions of isolated base-e exponentials with a linear exponent by applying the natural logarithm, the inverse identity, the logarithm power rule where needed, then linear algebra.
learner_operation: Read the signed coefficient and constant of the unknown in the exponent and the positive right-hand-side expression; derive the logarithmic value and isolate the requested unknown. The logarithm coefficient and constant in the response must follow those assignments.
reasoning_steps: Take ln of both sides of e^(a v+b)=R.
For integer powers or roots, use ln(B^p)=p ln(B).
Solve a v+b=ln(R) exactly; match an option or enter an equivalent expression.
response_contract: Observed radio fields have five full mathematical choices; q-263058 has a single blank field-1 after y=. Some captured questions and the canonical example have no fields. Do not infer a free-entry contract for those missing fields.
difficulty: Easy evidence is e^t=11; moderate q-263058 is e^(4-5y)=21; canonical e-4103 uses e^(x-3)=2^5; hard questions add root conversion. At requested moderate, signed linear exponents and integer RHS are directly grounded.
invariants: Base e; isolated exponential equals a positive constant expression.
A single real unknown occurs linearly in the exponent with nonzero coefficient.
Exact logarithmic response and corresponding natural-log worked method.
No extra isolation outside exponential, nonlinear unknown, approximate rounding, or logarithm domains requiring new case analysis.
